$comment: Cross-language SignableWrite canonical-CBOR conformance vector for #2455.
PROVENANCE: `canonical_cbor_hex` and `content_sha256_hex` were PRINTED BY
THE RUST ENCODER, not hand-written and not computed by either SDK. They
were produced by temporarily adding a #[test] that calls the production
helpers verbatim:
let content_hash = identity::attest::content_sha256(content);
let w = identity::sign::SignableWrite { .. };
let cbor = identity::sign::canonical_cbor_write(&w).unwrap();
and running `cargo test --lib <name> -- --nocapture`. The temporary test
was reverted; src/ is untouched by this change.
WHY: an SDK that signs a DIFFERENT byte sequence than the daemon verifies
produces a 403 that looks like a key-enrollment problem. Pinning the exact
envelope bytes against the Rust encoder is what makes the SDK's signature
trustworthy — a self-computed 'expected' value would prove nothing.
Ed25519 over identical bytes is deterministic (RFC 8032), so byte-equal
envelopes imply byte-equal signatures; the SDK suites additionally pin the
Ed25519 primitive against RFC 8032 TEST 3 (see rfc8032_test3 below).
KEY ORDER: RFC 8949 4.2.1 sorts map keys by ENCODED bytes (length first,
then bytewise), giving _dst, kind, title, agent_id, namespace, created_at,
content_sha256 for this fixed key set.
title: pg upgrade window
content: Postgres upgrade window is Sunday 02:00-04:00 UTC.

rfc8032_test3.$comment: RFC 8032 section 7.1 TEST 3 - pins the Ed25519 primitive itself against an external authority, independent of ai-memory.
